questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: All courses were taught in English (Master's level mathematics), and Charles University had a large number of interesting courses to choose from.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Charles University were a bit slow with sending the information needed about study start, but they did and everything was quite clear and very easy to navigate in.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: On the first day of the semester, there was an introductory day where I met all the other Erasmus students from my faculty, and we got our ISIC etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Charles University provided a 2-person room in a dormitory (17th of November dorm / Troja dorm), which was 20 minutes away from my university building. So I did not do anything myself. It was extremely cheap.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I shared kitchen with 2 others, but it was still quite dirty. The room was old fashioned, but big enough and practical. It was actually a room for two people, but I never got a room mate, so I had it all for myself. I know others who experienced the same.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It takes some time to go through all the bureaucracy, but it was not too difficult, and coordinators were good at answering mails. Just start in good time.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could always write my coordinator at UCPH or Charles University if I was in doubt about anything.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 5 out of 6 courses that I wanted, which is very lucky from what I hear from others. The first three weeks, I could switch courses so the course selection process was not stressful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: In practice, the stuff you put in your Learning Agreement is preliminary, and it will probably change.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: In general the courses had a level similar to UPCH, except for one course which was crazy difficult.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More chill vibe with the professors, and less formal and less bureaucracy. A bit more theoretical, and fewer problem sessions.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Commutative Algebra 6 ECTS
Curves and Function Fields 6 ECTS
Quantum Information 6 ECTS
Group Representations 5 ECTS
Algebraic Invariants in Knot Theory 4 ECTS
Formal Mathematics and Proof Assistants 3 ECTS

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Commutative Algebra was crazy difficult. Knot Theory was a bit more chill, and pretty cool. Formal Mathematics was a lot of guest lectures as well and a very easy exam. In general, I was happy with my courses.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Beer is cheap, but if you drink enough often enough, it adds up. It is super cheap in shops though.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Fast food is almost Danish prices. And Irish pubs are expensive. Food on restaurants and beers in general were cheaper than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had plans of using them, but I never did, and I never looked into it.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: ESN Prague arranges a lot of activities for socializing in the beginning. That was very nice.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go on some trips.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of nice day trips, also weekend trips. It is cheap to travel inside Czech Republic. Go to Cesky Krumlov and Bohemian Switzerland. And to Vienna or Krakow or something.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Almost everyone knows enough English, so don't worry about that. Aside from that, Prague is a very easy city to live in. The culture is not crazy different.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: A lot of them were curious to talk to me, and in general they were very nice. Also, there are a lot of international students who study in Prague for longer periods of time, and they are also great.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language is of course a barrier, but Google Translate's image feature made it a lot easier. Other than that, people in general are less motivated to help you, so if you need something, you need to be a bit more persistent.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: A lot less bureaucracy and way less formal.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
If you are in doubt, always say yes.
Prague has a lot of interesting areas. Try to experience as many as you can.
Prioritize the social life.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find someone with the same hobbies as you.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many amazing people and spending time with them in complete freedom without having to worry about work and duties from back home.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Going home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Exchange was probably my best decision. It is amazing to be together with so many people in the same boat as you and having so much free time to make friendships and explore a whole new city. And explore new sides of your own personality that are hidden back home. I have grown more confident in myself and have gotten a greater motivation for meeting new people back in Copenhagen as well. If you consider going, you really should go.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
